We've all been there. I gave myself a hair cut on a drunken night about 10 years ago. It turned out awfully.

Pro Tip-

Your hair will lift (from black) with bleach to red-orange, orange, yellow because of the way the natural pigments work. The lighter you go, the more the bleach opens the hair up, and the more stuff comes out. To minimize damage and get a better color after bleaching, you want to use a color that will neutralize the brassy naturally remaining pigments. For a "gold" blonde, lift to yellow and then apply a neutral to ash blonde color. Be careful with ash. It is best to play it safe and mix 1/2 ash blonde with 1/2 neutral to avoid turning hair green/blue/"mousy" (mostly visible under bad lighting). If you just want a lighter brown, lift to an orange-yellow. Red tones usually only need slight lifting to orange. Ash/neutral tones colors neutralize the brassiness and will usually still appear "gold." Using a warm/gold tone on bleached hair with natural remaining pigment may blend it (if starting from a lighter natural hair color), but often cannot compensate for the natural pigment and will have a brassy end result. The darker the natural hair, the stronger your natural pigment, and the more brassiness you will see when lifting. Also you cannot lift color with color. Color can lighten natural hair (no bleaching required), but it cannot lighten colored hair.

Also your developer volume = levels of lift. If you are a level 2 (one step lighter than black), level 2 dye w/10 or 20 volume will tone and cover grays without lightening (use 20 volume for grays). Level 3 dye with 25 volume will give you one level of lift. Level 4 dye with 30 volume gives you 3 levels of lift to a level 5. Level 6 dye with 40 volume gives 4 levels of lift to level 6. This is kind of a standard formulation method. It gets more complex. You could put a level 10 high lift color with 40 volume on and probably get a nice level 7/8. Lifting with color is usually less harsh on the hair cuticle because it deposits color as it lifts. Also in South America and Asia you can get level 50 & 60 developer. Do not use anything above 30 on your scalp though! Lifting twice with level 20 is much gentler than lifting once with 40 an burning your scalp (and hair).
